dimensions.note: Bank of Korea's 알기 쉬운 경제이야기 series (published since 2005, separately pitched at elementary/middle/high-school/general readers) frames economic ideas through a recurring family's conversations and folk/fairy-tale economic episodes rather than expository definition. This independently corroborates the concrete-before-abstract framing trait already found in ref:econoi-childrens-economic-newspaper's articles, from a different institution (a central bank publication programme, not a newspaper) and a different concrete device (an ongoing family-conversation frame plus retold folk stories, vs. econoi's Q&A-and-한자어-decomposition device). This record was assigned holdout before reading and no new trait is derived from it beyond confirming the one above; it is not used to originate a trait.
dimensions.evidence: Publisher description of the elementary-level volume: "한은이네 가족의 대화와 여러 가지 이야기를 재미있게 읽다 보면 여러분들은 자연스럽게 경제를 익히고, 경제적으로 생각할 수 있는 힘을 키울 수 있습니다." (Reading 한은이's family's conversations and various stories, you naturally pick up economics and build the capacity to think economically.)

dimensions.note: Could not verify the actual body prose (sentence length, clause depth, vocabulary tier, or whether stated uncertainty survives simplification) because the publication is distributed as a PDF booklet that this evaluation could not extract text from. The finding above is limited to the structural device (family-narrative frame) as described in the publisher's own front-matter, not to sentence-level craft. This gap should be closed before any of this record's evidence is used to derive (rather than merely validate) a trait.

strengths: Independent-institution corroboration of concrete-before-abstract framing: a central-bank publication programme reaches for the same move (attach an abstract economic idea to an ongoing, familiar narrative) that a dedicated children's economics newspaper reaches for, via a different concrete device.

Explicit audience tiering by depth, not by a different voice per tier: the same series title and framing device ('경제이야기') is republished at elementary/middle/high-school/general levels, which is itself evidence that this institution treats audience as a depth dial on one editorial approach rather than a wholesale register swap into a separate 'child voice' per book.
weaknesses: The named family ('한은이', '중은이' and parents) and the specific retold folk-tale episodes are this publication's own recognizable content; the transferable lesson is the structural device (a persistent, familiar narrative frame carrying the abstraction), never the characters or the specific stories — do_not_copy on the concrete instantiation.

Sentence-level Korean (length, clause depth, hedging under uncertainty) is unverified here — this record validates a structural trait only and must not be read as validating anything about prose-level craft.
